outcome: The bound was settled in 1994 by Dias da Silva and Hamidoune, before the window. Since 26 January 2024 nothing has changed the statement's status: a single-author elementary re-proof appeared on arXiv on 19 May 2026 (Yang), and a Lean 4 formalisation of the bound for prime p was posted on the Erdős problems forum on 31 December 2025 (plby/lean-proofs, with Aristotle as formal author and ChatGPT credited as informal author). Several 2024-2026 papers study neighbouring questions (inverse problem, Z_p^2 variant, Lev's matching conjecture, h-fold sumsets with large sets, general abelian groups), and none of them is the bound itself.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone. (a) A universal claim over every prime p (the bullet says prime; composite moduli are not asked). (b) Over every nonempty finite A contained in Z/pZ. (c) The lower bound |2^A| >= min{p, 2|A|-3}, where 2^A (the restricted sumset with two summands) is the set of sums a+b with a, b in A and a not equal to b. The one quantity named is |2^A|. The bound has two regimes inside the min: for 2|A|-3 < p it is the number 2|A|-3, and otherwise it says the restricted sumset is all of Z/pZ. The bullet does not ask for the equality cases, the inverse characterisation, or any other group (abelian or otherwise); those are separate questions.

events.what_happened: J. A. Dias da Silva and Y. O. Hamidoune, 'Cyclic spaces for Grassmann derivatives and additive theory', Bull. London Math. Soc. 26(2) (1994) 140-146 (DOI 10.1112/blms/26.2.140 as cited by later papers). I could not open the paper: the DOI page returned HTTP 429 and the Encyclopedia of Mathematics page returned HTTP 502, so the scope below rests on secondary statements. Wikipedia's restricted-sumset article says the conjecture 'was first confirmed by J. A. Dias da Silva and Y. O. Hamidoune in 1994'. Du and Pan's abstract (arXiv 2403.03549) and Yang's introduction (as summarised by my fetch tool) state the k-fold bound |k^A| >= min{p(F), k|A| - k^2 + 1} for a finite nonempty A in a field F, which at k = 2 and F = Z/pZ is the bullet. The erdosproblems.com page for #476 says 'Solved in the affirmative by da Silva and Hamidoune [dSHa94].' Method, per secondary sources: exterior algebra and the representation theory of the symmetric group. Date given is the journal year; I did not establish whether an earlier preprint carried the argument.
events.delivers: The full bullet: for every prime p and every nonempty A in Z/pZ, |2^A| >= min{p, 2|A|-3}, as the k = 2 case of the k-fold bound (secondary statements; original not read).
events.remains: Nothing of the bullet's statement. The equality cases and any inverse characterisation are not addressed by this paper as reported.

Number Theory 56(2) (1996) 404-417 (February 1996 per the bibliographic record). Their polynomial-method route uses the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz and gives a tight lower bound on restricted sums a_0 + ... + a_k with a_i in A_i distinct, in Z/pZ. Secondary sources (Wikipedia, erdosproblems, Lean docstring) credit it as the proof of the general case and as the route to the bullet; Wikipedia dates the work 1995-1996, and Yang's paper cites Alon-Nathanson-Ruzsa (1995). I give 1995 as the first-argument year, which is an inference from those citations, not a verified preprint date. The exact two-set bound in their paper was not read (the PDF returned unreadable binary; the publisher page returned HTTP 403).

events.what_happened: G. Karolyi, 'The Erdos-Heilbronn problem in Abelian groups', Israel J. Math. 139 (2004) 349-359 (DOI 10.1007/bf02787556 per an OpenAIRE record). Not opened. Per a survey and a 2012 arXiv timeline quoted by search: for every finite abelian group G and nonempty finite A, |A^A| >= min{p(G), 2|A|-3}, where p(G) is the least order of a nonzero element. For G = Z/pZ this contains the bullet. Karolyi also proved an inverse theorem for Z/pZ (for |A| >= 5 and p > 2|A|-3, equality holds iff A is an arithmetic progression), as cited by Balister-Wheeler and Jayasuriya-Reich-Wheeler. Date is the journal year; preprint date not checked.
events.delivers: The bullet as the case G = Z/pZ, plus the generalisation to all finite abelian groups (secondary statement; not read).
events.remains: Nothing of the bullet. The inverse characterisation is a separate question.

The quoted forms disagree on '>' versus '>=' and on a sigma-twisted variant, so I record the statement as a secondary report only.

events.what_happened: V. Vu and M. Wood, 'The inverse Erdos-Heilbronn problem', Electron. J. Combin. 16 (2009) #R100, published 7 August 2009 per the journal record. Not opened. Per the abstract as quoted by search: under the extra assumption |A| <= (1/2 - 1/log^c p)p, their main result has the Dias da Silva-Hamidoune theorem and Karolyi's theorem as corollaries, giving 'purely combinatorial proofs for the Erdos-Heilbronn conjecture'. Their main subject is the inverse (structural) question for small doubling.

events.what_happened: S. Du and H. Pan, 'The restricted sumsets in finite abelian groups', arXiv 2403.03549, submitted 6 March 2024 (single version). The arXiv page says 'Accepted by the Israel Journal of Mathematics' with no volume. Abstract page read: for k >= 2, a nonempty subset A of a finite abelian group G with |G| > 1, the k-fold restricted sumset k^A satisfies |k^A| >= min{p(G), k|A| - k^2 + 1}, where p(G) is the least prime divisor of |G|. For G = Z/pZ and k = 2 this is the bullet. The paper is in the window but its bullet case is an instance of a more general theorem.
events.revisions: v1 only (6 March 2024). Accepted by the Israel Journal of Mathematics per arXiv page.

events.remains: Nothing of the bullet, which it contains as a special case. Its content for the bullet is not new; the bullet was settled in 1994.

events.what_happened: Shengning Zhang, 'On the Elementary Proof of the Inverse Erdos-Heilbronn Problem', arXiv 2408.13755, submitted 25 August 2024 (single version, no journal listed). Abstract page read. It concerns the inverse problem for the restricted sumset of two sets A and B that need not be equal. It gives an elementary proof for the integers and partial results toward Z/pZ, without the polynomial method. A snippet of the paper states that for p >= |A|+|B|-2, |A+B| = |A|+|B|-3 holds iff A = B with one of several structures (small sizes, or an arithmetic progression for |A| >= 5).
events.delivers: Elementary proofs for the inverse problem over Z and partial results over Z/pZ, characterising equality cases of restricted two-set bounds.
events.remains: The bullet's lower bound itself, which this paper does not state or change.
events.direction: Does not address the bullet's inequality. It concerns when equality holds in a related bound; for Z/pZ only partial results are reported (quoted from the abstract page: 'some partial results that contributes to the elementary proof of the problem in Z/pZ').

events.what_happened: Jacinda Terkel, 'Restricted sums of sets of cardinality 2p+1 in Z_p^2', arXiv 2410.00143. Versions: v1 30 September 2024, v2 4 October 2024, v3 17 October 2024, v4 22 October 2024, v5 23 September 2025 (marked withdrawn), v6 6 February 2026 (current). Abstract page read: for prime p >= 5 and A in Z_p^2 with 2p+1 elements, the restricted sumset has at least 4p elements. The author calls it the first progress in over two decades on a variant studied by Eliahou and Kervaire.

events.remains: The bullet, which concerns subsets of Z/pZ with the bound 2|A|-3, is not touched. Different group and set size.

events.what_happened: Minghui Ouyang, 'On restricted sumsets with bounded degree relations', arXiv 2503.09121 (v1 12 March 2025; v2 20 August 2025; v3 4 September 2025). Journal: Mathematika 71(4) (2025) e70045. Abstract page read: for subsets A, B of F_p and a relation R, the restricted sumset A +_R B is sums a+b with (a,b) not in R. Lev conjectured that for a matching R with |A|+|B| <= p, |A +_R B| >= |A|+|B|-3; the author proves this when |A|+|B| <= (1-eps)p and p > p_0(eps). The paper says that with R equal to equality the problem is 'the famous Erdos-Heilbronn problem'.
events.revisions: v1 12 Mar 2025; v2 20 Aug 2025; v3 4 Sep 2025; published Mathematika 71(4) (2025) e70045.
events.delivers: Lev's matching conjecture in the range |A|+|B| <= (1-eps)p for large p. My reading, not stated in the paper: with R the diagonal on A (a matching of A with itself), this gives the bullet for |A| <= (1-eps)p/2 and p > p_0(eps). That range was already covered in 1994.
events.remains: The bullet's statement for |A| above (1-eps)p/2 is not reached by this result; for the bullet itself it adds no new range. Lev's general conjecture for matchings remains open outside the range.

events.what_happened: A Lean 4 formalisation of the bullet's statement. In plby/lean-proofs (src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos476.lean), restrictedSumset A is the image of pairs (x, y) in A x A with x not equal to y under x + y, and the theorem erdos_476 states, for p prime and A : Finset (ZMod p), (restrictedSumset A).card >= min (2 * A.card - 3) p. The header lists informal authors J. A. Dias da Silva, Yahya Ould Hamidoune, Noga Alon, Melvyn B. Nathanson, Imre Z. Ruzsa and 'ChatGPT', and formal authors 'Aristotle' and 'Boris Alexeev'. It says: 'We proved the Erdos-Heilbronn inequality in F_p.' and 'We followed the proof outline provided, formalizing the necessary lemmas about Lagrange interpolation, the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz, and properties of restricted sumsets.' On erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/476, BorisAlexeev posted on 31 December 2025 at 05:09: 'Aristotle auto-formalized a different solution to this problem, using the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz', and 'The final statement was written by Aristotle itself, but it looks good to me.' The post links a Markdown write-up and an online type-checker. Separately, google-deepmind/formal-conjectures FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/476.lean (copyright 2026) states the problem with the declaration sorry'd and the proof linked to plby. The formalised argument is the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz route of Alon-Nathanson-Ruzsa, not a new argument.

events.what_happened: Vivekanand Goswami and Raj Kumar Mistri, 'Restricted set addition in finite abelian groups', arXiv 2603.04572, v1 4 March 2026, v2 23 May 2026. Abstract page read: for h >= 4, a threshold alpha_h (the positive root of 3^(h-2)x^(h-1) + x - 1), and odd n sufficiently large, any A with |A| >= alpha n has h^A = G, where h^A is the set of sums of h distinct elements. The bullet (Z/pZ, two summands, sets of size about 2p) is not the setting.
events.delivers: For h >= 4, a covering statement for h-fold restricted sumsets of large subsets of abelian groups of odd order.
events.remains: The bullet, which concerns h = 2 and all sizes in Z/pZ.
events.direction: Different question (large sets, h-fold, general abelian groups of odd order).

events.what_happened: Guanzhong Yang, 'Linear Algebraic Method and the Erdos-Heilbronn Conjecture', arXiv 2605.19542, single author, submitted 19 May 2026, v1 only, 10 pages, math.CO and math.RA. The abstract says the note develops Das's linear algebraic method and gives 'a new elementary proof of the Alon-Nathanson-Ruzsa theorem for restricted sumsets, which implies the Erdos-Heilbronn conjecture'. Main theorem (Theorem 3.1), as read from the arXiv HTML through a summarising fetch: for nonempty A, B in Z/pZ with |A| not equal to |B|, |A dotplus B| >= min{p, |A|+|B|-2}, where A dotplus B = {a+b : a in A, b in B, a not equal to b}. Corollary 3.1 (Erdos-Heilbronn): remove a_0 from A to get A' = A minus {a_0}; then A dotplus A' is contained in A dotplus A, so |A dotplus A| >= |A dotplus A'| >= min{p, 2|A|-3}. The bullet follows. Affiliation given as Imperial College London in the HTML summary. No journal reference, no acknowledgements, no AI mention.
events.revisions: v1 only, submitted 19 May 2026, as of the abstract page read.
events.delivers: The full bullet for every prime p and every nonempty finite A in Z/pZ, via a stronger two-set bound for |A| not equal to |B| (as read from the summarised HTML).
events.remains: Nothing of the bullet. The author presents the result as a new proof of the Alon-Nathanson-Ruzsa theorem, not as a resolution.
events.time_since_posted: about 4.8 months (19 May 2026 to 11 Oct 2026); no review, comment, journal record or citing paper found
events.directly_checkable: The argument is short linear algebra over F_p (Vandermonde matrices, solvability of linear systems). The reduction from Theorem 3.1 to the bullet can be checked by hand from the statement given above. I did not check the proof of Theorem 3.1 itself.
events.doubts: The paper asserts A dotplus A = A dotplus A' is 'straightforward to verify' (per the summarised HTML). Only the inclusion A dotplus A' contained in A dotplus A is needed for the bound, and it is immediate, so the bound survives; the stated equality is unargued and not used. I identify no error. The paper is single-author, has no journal record and no acknowledgements. The text I read was a summary, so the exact wording of the corollary and of Theorem 3.1 is unverified.
events.direction: Confirms the bullet's statement, via a stronger two-set bound for |A| not equal to |B|.

disputes.summary: In the Alexeev formalisation writeups, ChatGPT and Lean are listed as coauthors. In the comments on the Xena guest post, Tony Feng (12 Dec 2025) wrote: 'I found the decision to include ChatGPT and Lean as coauthors to be rather curious.' This is a general dispute about author credit for these writeups, not one specific to this problem. The Erdos 476 file credits 'ChatGPT' in the same way.

summary: The bullet was settled in 1994 by Dias da Silva and Hamidoune (Bull. LMS 26(2), 140-146), before the window. I could not open that paper (DOI and encyclopaedia pages returned HTTP 429 and 502), so its scope rests on secondary statements that agree with one another: Wikipedia's restricted-sumset article, Du and Pan's abstract, the erdosproblems.com page for #476 ('Solved in the affirmative by da Silva and Hamidoune'), Yang's introduction and the Lean docstring. Alon, Nathanson and Ruzsa (J. Number Theory 1996; first argument probably 1995, which I could not confirm) gave the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz proof, and Karolyi (2004), Balister and Wheeler (2009), Vu and Wood (2009, a combinatorial route only for |A| <= (1/2 - 1/log^c p)p) and Feher and Nagy (arXiv 2016, equivariant cohomology) are earlier generalisations or re-proofs. Within the window, the nearest items are: Du and Pan (March 2024), a general abelian-group theorem that contains the bullet as G = Z/pZ; Zhang (August 2024), an inverse problem; Terkel (September 2024), a Z_p^2 variant; Ouyang (March 2025), Lev's matching conjecture, which read with R = equality gives a range of the bullet already known (my inference); and Goswami and Mistri (March 2026), h-fold sums of large sets. Two events restate the bullet itself. The first is Yang's arXiv preprint of 19 May 2026, a single-author elementary linear-algebra proof of the Alon-Nathanson-Ruzsa theorem, from which the bullet follows through a corollary. It carries no AI disclosure, no journal record, and I found no review or citing work. Its corollary asserts an equality that it does not need. The second is the Lean formalisation in plby/lean-proofs, posted to the Erdos forum on 31 December 2025 by Boris Alexeev. The file is sorry-free on my reading (summarised fetch, not compiled by me), and lists Aristotle as formal author and ChatGPT as informal author, with the phrase 'We followed the proof outline provided'. The formalised argument is the 1995/96 Combinatorial Nullstellensatz route, so this is a machine check of a known theorem, and the source does not say what ChatGPT contributed. The forum thread has one comment and no replies. The erdosproblems.com page, last edited 30 Sep 2025, credits no AI. The formal-conjectures stub for erdos_476 has sorry on its declaration, with the proof linked to plby. The AlphaProof Nexus results repository lists nine Erdos problems (12, 26, 125, 138, 152, 741(i), 741(ii), 846), and 476 is not among them. The live Wikipedia list, read in full, has no Erdos-Heilbronn entry. A mirror's claim about a 2024 talk-page removal request is unverified and I have not relied on it. The frozen January 2024 revision itself was not checked. Close calls: whether Yang's preprint and the Lean file count as resolutions or as re-proofs (both re-prove a settled bound and change no quantity the bullet asks for); whether the ChatGPT credit is load-bearing (it is the only AI attribution on the mathematics, and it is unexplained).
competing_reading: The Lean docstring credits ChatGPT as an informal author and says the formalised proof followed 'the proof outline provided', so one could read this as an AI system supplying a load-bearing argument for the bullet in December 2025. Against that: the outline is the 1995/96 human Combinatorial Nullstellensatz route, the source does not say who supplied the outline, and the forum post credits Aristotle with the formalisation, not the idea. A second reading treats Yang's May 2026 preprint as a fresh resolution of an open bullet. Against that: the bullet was settled in 1994, the preprint describes itself as a new proof of Alon-Nathanson-Ruzsa, and the frozen list was already out of date by 2026. A third reading takes Ouyang's Lev-conjecture result as bearing on the bullet. My reading is that it contributes only a range already known. The paper itself does not state the bullet.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of Dias da Silva and Hamidoune (1994) and of Alon, Nathanson and Ruzsa (1996), to confirm the exact bound and its scope, and whether an earlier preprint carried the argument. (2) The plby/lean-proofs git history and its ErdosProblems/Erdos476.md write-up. These would show who wrote the proof outline, when the file first appeared, and whether any proof step is sorry-free in a verbatim read. Compiling the file under Lean v4.29.1 would settle the machine check. (3) Yang's PDF, to confirm Theorem 3.1, the corollary's wording, and whether the equality A dotplus A = A dotplus A' is claimed; and any later review or citation of the paper. (4) A statement from Boris Alexeev or the Erdos forum saying what ChatGPT produced for #476. (5) The frozen January 2024 Wikipedia revision, to confirm the bullet's wording there.
